- [FACT] The user was diagnosed with a small pulmonary embolism in March.
- [PREFERENCE] The user wants to learn more about pulmonary embolism and how to prevent it from happening again.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provides a definition of pulmonary embolism (PE) as a blockage in one of the arteries in the lungs caused by a blood clot.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant lists causes and risk factors for PE, including deep vein thrombosis (DVT), immobility, inherited blood-clotting disorders, cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, heart failure, pregnancy, hormone replacement therapy, and age.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant describes common symptoms of PE, including sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, coughing up blood, fatigue, rapid heartbeat, and lightheadedness.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant outlines the diagnosis process for PE, including medical history, imaging tests, and blood tests.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explains treatment options for PE, including anticoagulation therapy, thrombolytic therapy, and supportive care.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provides prevention strategies for PE, such as staying active, maintaining a healthy weight, avoiding prolonged immobility, staying hydrated, and managing underlying medical conditions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant emphasizes the importance of follow-up with a healthcare provider for monitoring and adjusting treatment plans.
